newsitem.title: DUBAI: Arab League urges greater EU Mideast peace role.
newsitem.headline: Arab League urges greater EU Mideast peace role.

text.p: The Arab League on Monday called for a greater European Union role in the Middle East peace process.
Esmat Abdel Meguid, secretary-general of the 22-member league, said in a message ahead of a conference on European and Arab cooperation on the peace process:

"It is our hope that member states of the EU will play in the peace process a far greater role in line with the weight of Europe on the international domain and the volume of European interest in the Middle East."
Abdel Meguid's message from the Cairo-based league was delivered on his behalf at a news conference in Dubai, where he is due to head Arab delegations to the three-day conference starting April 3.
European Commission vice president Manuel Marin and the EU's special envoy to the peace process, Miguel Moratinos, are among participants from the European side.

One of the main issues scheduled for discussion will be the expansion to the six Arab oil states of the Gulf Cooperation Council -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Bahrain -- of some existing political, economic and cultural programmes under the EU-Mediterranean partnership.
The partnership already includes eight Arab countries and four non-Arab Mediterranean states.
There will be "no Israeli participation, no observers," said Saeed Salman, one of the Dubai conference organisers. "This is Euro-Arab purely."
